title: Retro notes (raw) — Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated fleet bring-up)
content:
Doc: raw retro notes for the “Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)”.

NOTE: this is NOT the polished retro for Confluence. This is the messy capture + action item scratchpad.

Date/time
- 2025-03-08 (Fri) 10:00–11:00 PT

Facilitator
- Vanessa Ortiz

Notes taken by
- Kira Thompson

Attendees (partial; whoever showed)
- Infra/Fleet: Vanessa Ortiz, Gabe Wilson, Harish Reddy, Nina Petrova (drop-in)
- SRE: Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Miles Thornton (first 20m)
- Platform/CP/Routing: Ethan Park, Ravi Menon (drop-in), Jordan Lee (drop-in)
- Observability: Allison Grant
- Security: (none live) — follow up async with Marcus Lin/Kevin Osei on remaining items

Goal reminder
- Reduce time-to-ready for Dedicated bring-up and make it less “hand-offy” (SRE to Infra to Platform ping pong).
- “Ready” means routing will actually use it (no more ‘cluster exists’ == ‘ready’ confusion).

What we shipped (rough)
- Provisioning state machine + persisted transitions (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed)
- Structured stage events + correlation IDs in logs/metrics
- Operator CLI (trigger runs, re-run stage, dry-run)
- Initial readiness gates: GPU health + network/DNS/TLS checks + runtime smoke
- Perf-canary ‘readiness suite’ integrated into validation (minimal bench)
- Time-to-ready dashboard + stuck-stage alerts (first cut)
- Ready gating in routing integration (routing ignores anything not Ready)
- Break-glass override for config validation (admin-only, audit logged)

Quick numbers (VERY rough, from Aisha/Jamal; confirm w/ dashboard)
- Baseline (last 10 bring-ups): p50 ~18–22h, p95 ~48–72h
  - main culprits: imaging variability, Terraform retries, bootstrap misconfigs, manual waiting / unclear ownership
- Pilot (staging x2, prod customer expansion x1):
  - best run: ~6.5h end-to-end
  - typical run: ~9–12h
  - worst run: ~20h (stuck in Bootstrapping due to helm values footgun + retries)
- Biggest win: fewer “silent” stalls; we can see which stage and who owns it.

What went well (keep doing)
1) State machine + explicit ownership
- Having explicit stages + one “current stage” ended the Slack archaeology.
- Oncall/SRE liked that they could say “it’s Imaging owned by Infra” vs “it’s somewhere in the void”.
- The correlation ID plumbing mattered more than expected (made log hunting actually feasible).

2) Ready semantics got clarified (routing)
- Platform + SRE alignment: Validating is NOT usable.
- Routing only consumes Ready capacity. Good safety default.
- Follow-up decision captured in Slack thread; should be in runbook + customer language too.

3) Perf-canary as a gate (even minimal)
- Caught 1 case where runtime smoke passed but perf was clearly off (bad batch settings + GPU clock weirdness?).
- Having a simple pass/fail summary JSON is operator friendly.

4) Observability improvements shipped fast
- Dashboards came online early enough to iterate during pilot.
- Stage histograms + ‘stuck stage’ alerts reduced manual polling.

5) CLI helped operators (even with rough edges)
- Dry-run saved time during the staging enablement checklist.
- Ability to re-run validation only = huge for iteration speed.

6) Cross-team collaboration was real
- Infra/SRE/Platform actually had shared threads instead of separate threads.
- Vanessa facilitating with “single source of truth” links kept us moving.

What hurt / didn’t go well (be honest)
1) Imaging step variability is still our #1 timeline risk
- Region + SKU differences; timeouts on one region looked like artifact mirror slowness.
- Retries helped but also extended wall-clock; we need smarter fallback (alternate mirror / prewarm / caching).
- We still don’t have clean “imaging done” definition (image applied? reboot verified? GPU driver loaded? k8s join?).

2) Terraform apply failures: quota/IAM/edge cases
- Still too many “apply failed” due to missing perms / quota not preflighted.
- INT-1044 was painful because it was avoidable (permission drift between staging/prod roles).
- Need preflight checks + clearer error messages.

3) Bootstrap failures were noisy and confusing
- The incident thread (Bootstrapping stuck) was basically “helm values misconfig” + unclear which chart value caused it.
- Retries sometimes masked the root cause (kept cycling, no one saw the first failure line).
- We need better error categorization + surfacing first failure cause + link to runbook section.

4) Race condition: Ready set too early
- We had the bug where control plane marked Ready before perf-canary completed.
- Fixed, but it spooked leadership + customer success.
- Takeaway: gating logic needs tests with failure injection + “don’t regress” guard.

5) Config validation broke an edge-case config (policy gates)
- Good that it prevented a real misconfig, but it also blocked one legitimate use case.
- Break-glass exists, but we need a better “this is blocked because…” message + migration guidance.
- INT-1047: ask for allowlist w/ expiry + audit trail (so we don’t normalize break-glass).

6) Alerting policy still fuzzy (paging vs ticket)
- Some stuck-stage alerts paged too aggressively early in pilot.
- “Failure rate” thresholds need stage-specific tuning (imaging vs validation are different).
- Ownership boundaries: who gets paged if Bootstrapping fails due to helm? SRE? Platform? Infra?

7) Documentation lagged behind code
- Operators complained the runbook was “out of date relative to CLI flags”.
- We had multiple sources (Drive checklist + Confluence runbook + Slack snippet).
- Need a single authoritative runbook link printed by the CLI.

8) Comms / expectation setting with Sales/CS
- CS asked for new ETA language; we did not have crisp wording for “ready” vs “provisioned” vs “validating”.
- When we had the bootstrapping incident, the update cadence was inconsistent.

Notable incidents / surprises (for memory)
- Bootstrapping stuck due to helm values misconfig (pilot). Mitigation: pause pipeline, fix values, re-run bootstrap stage. Follow-up: add lint rule + better error message.
- Imaging timeouts in region X (artifact mirror). Workaround: manual mirror switch (documented in Slack). Need real fix.
- Duplicate Slack bot stage updates (noise) (INT ticket exists).
- Dashboard variables didn’t populate for new pool IDs initially (template mismatch).

Root causes (themes)
- “Unknown unknowns” become “known knowns” once we standardize stage boundaries + events.
- Many failures are not complicated technically, but we lacked: (a) preflights, (b) crisp errors, (c) one place to look.
- We still have too many implicit dependencies (IAM, quotas, mirrors) that are not validated early.

What we should do next cycle (candidate follow-ups)
(These are NOT all committed; needs grooming)

P0 (next sprint / immediate hardening)
- Add preflight checks before Terraform apply:
  - quota availability, IAM permissions sanity, required artifacts reachable, required DNS zones configured
  - output a single “preflight report” w/ pass/fail + next steps
- Bootstrap error surfacing:
  - capture first-failure line + persist it (don’t lose it to retries)
  - map common failures → explicit categories (dns/tls, helm schema, authz, image mismatch)
- Imaging step definition + measurement:
  - add sub-metrics: download time, apply time, reboot time, driver verify time, k8s join time
- Make CLI print canonical links:
  - dashboard link, runbook link, Linear project link, logs search link with correlation ID
- Add regression tests around Ready gating (esp. perf-canary ordering)

P1 (should do)
- Config validation improvements:
  - clearer error messages + suggested fix
  - allowlist mechanism with explicit expiry + owner + reason
  - small migration tool / “config doctor” mode in CLI
- Drift detection rollout:
  - ensure it’s non-noisy (don’t create drift for benign diffs)
  - add ‘acknowledge drift’ workflow?
- Alert policy tuning:
  - stage-specific stuck thresholds
  - default to ticket for non-critical failures; page only if customer-impacting or blocked >X hours
- Imaging fallback:
  - alternate mirror selection + automatic fallback
  - prewarm images in region for expected SKUs (coordinate w/ capacity planning)

P2 (nice to have)
- Better customer-facing status mapping:
  - translate internal stages to 2–3 external statuses (e.g., Provisioning / Validating / Ready)
  - standard message templates for CS
- “Single pane of glass” run page:
  - one URL shows stage timeline, events, retries, current owner, and next action
- Add a small “capacity bring-up post-check” that verifies routing saw it and traffic can be dialed up safely

Decisions captured (make sure they land somewhere more permanent)
- Routing will only use Ready capacity (not Validating). If perf-canary fails, pool stays out of routing.
- Break-glass is permitted but must be admin-only + audit logged + alert hook. We should treat it as an exception path with follow-up.

Action items (draft; assign owners in Linear)
- [Vanessa/Gabe] Create Linear tickets for imaging sub-metrics + mirror fallback design.
- [Rafael/Aisha] Propose alert matrix: per-stage thresholds, paging vs ticket, ownership mapping.
- [Ethan/Ravi] Add integration test coverage for Ready gating + perf-canary ordering; include failure injection.
- [Benji/Jordan] Update validation error copy + draft allowlist-with-expiry approach.
- [Kira] Consolidate runbook + checklist; ensure CLI prints the correct links; remove duplicate/outdated Drive doc once Confluence is final.
- [Allison/Sergio] Fix dashboard template variables for new pool IDs and add “run timeline” widget.

Shout-outs
- Gabe: correlation IDs + events plumbing (painful but worth it)
- Aisha: got the dashboard + metric naming to a usable place quickly
- Ethan: pushed on Ready semantics and got routing gating shipped
- Harish: pilot execution + keeping operators calm during hiccups

Parking lot / open questions
- Do we want stage-level SLOs (budgets per stage) as formal SLOs, or just internal targets?
- How do we handle heterogeneous SKUs without hardcoding (esp. perf-canary thresholds)? Per-SKU baseline library?
- When we “pause” a run, what’s the SLA for resuming / who owns it? (avoid indefinite limbo)
- Should the pipeline create/attach a ticket automatically on first failure (with context), even if it self-retries?

Links to paste into the polished retro later
- Confluence overview + stage definitions
- ADR-0142 + ADR-0143
- Linear project ENG-2741 and the follow-up epic (TBD)

End.
